text:
**Short answer: LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice for most buyers.** NMC only makes sense if weight is your top priority or you're getting a deeply discounted unit for light use.

**Where LiFePO4 wins**
- **Cycle life:** LFP stations are typically rated 2,000-6,000 cycles, versus roughly 500-1,000 for NMC. In one comparison, daily use gets you about 8 years from a 3,000-cycle LFP unit versus about 1.4 years from a 500-cycle NMC unit ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)).
- **Failure behavior:** Lab studies on small cells found LFP burns cooler and less violently when it fails (e.g., peak ~259°C vs ~731°C in one test). LFP isn't fireproof, and one study found it hit thermal runaway earlier under overcharge, so the battery management system still matters ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/), [UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)).
- **Cost over time:** One site's data shows a median of $0.55/Wh for LFP vs $0.95/Wh for NMC, and cost per rated cycle is far lower for LFP ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).
- **Availability:** Nearly all current models are LFP. In one database, 121 of 128 models are LFP ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).

**Where NMC wins (and how much)**
- NMC cells are denser (about 200-250 Wh/kg vs ~146 for LFP in one study), but finished stations narrow the gap a lot because the case, inverter, and fans weigh the same either way. One database found a median of 39.2 Wh/lb for NMC vs 35.5 for LFP, only about 10% apart. Another found about 16%. In some cases an LFP station was lighter per Wh than an NMC one ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)).
- Some sources claim 20-30% weight differences, but those are more generic estimates than measured stations.

**Caveats**
- **Cold weather:** Chemistry matters less than you'd think. Most LFP and NMC stations alike won't charge below 32°F. Check the manual's charging range.
- **Read cycle claims carefully:** "3,000 cycles to 70%" promises less than "to 80%," and test conditions vary by brand.
- **Occasional use:** If you only cycle it a few times a year for outages, calendar aging matters more than cycle count, and either chemistry can work.
- **Check the chemistry:** Some product pages don't state it, so verify before buying.

**Quick guide**
- Daily/solar/van/off-grid use → LiFePO4
- Home backup, indoors → LiFePO4
- Weight-critical, rare use → compare specific models; NMC may be lighter

**An LFP example:** The [BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2) is a 2,073.6 Wh LiFePO4 station with a 2,600 W inverter and a 6,000+ cycle rating, listed at $899. The listing says code AFF5OFF takes $44.95 off, bringing it to $854.05. It isn't expandable and weighs 24.2 kg (about 53 lb), so it's better for home backup than portability. The link is an affiliate link, so the retailer pays a commission at no cost to you. The code was tested on 2026-10-24, but the checkout price is what counts.

If you tell me your use case (outage backup, camping, van, etc.) and what you need to run, I can suggest a size and specific models.
